name: Haptic-vision cath.
group: Boston Children's Hospital / Harvard Medical School, Pediatric Cardiac Bioengineering Lab (G. Fagogenis, P. E. Dupont)
devices_driven: its own concentric-tube robotic catheter (three precurved superelastic tubes, OD 2.77 / 2.40 / 1.875 mm, Table 1) carrying the haptic-vision sensor; tools pass through the innermost tube (occluder on a wire inside a delivery cannula, Fig. 6)
n_dof_detail: N.R. as a number: the drive rotates and telescopically extends three tubes relative to each other, forming two telescoping sections (Robotic catheter design; Table 1; movie S1)
translation_detail: other: concentric-tube drive at the tube bases rotates and telescopically extends three precurved superelastic tubes (Robotic catheter design)
rotation_detail: concentric-tube drive rotates each tube at its base (Robotic catheter design)
device_range: tube OD 1.875-2.77 mm; sensor: 8 mm silicone optical window with 2.5 mm working channel (Table 1; Haptic vision sensor design)
force_sensing: no force sensor: tissue contact is inferred from the haptic-vision image (1 mm^3 NanEye CMOS camera + LED in an 8 mm silicone window); tip force set by the contact duty cycle (Fig. 1, Fig. 7)
haptics_leader: Touch (3D Systems) six-DOF joystick for the teleoperated comparator; force feedback N.R. (Computer software design)
imaging_compat: tip camera (haptic vision) for navigation; ultrasound monitor in the OR set-up (Fig. 2B); fluoroscopy N.R.
sterility: drive system draped in plastic in the OR (Fig. 2B); valve and flush system at the inner tube's proximal end keeps air out of the lumen (Robotic catheter design)
validation_detail: in vivo, Yorkshire swine 84.3 +- 4.7 kg with a custom leaky bioprosthetic aortic valve, transapical access: apex to annulus 5 animals / 90 autonomous trials (teleop 3 / 9, manual 3 / 13); circumnavigation 3 animals / 65 trials; to the leak 5 animals / 83 trials; occluder deployment 8/11 autonomous, 7/9 teleop, 11/13 manual (Results, In vivo experiments); ex vivo pressurized porcine heart for software testing (Fig. 5)
key_numbers: autonomous 99% (89/90) apex to annulus; 95% (79/83) to leak; 66% (43/65) for annulus following; time 39+-17 s vs 34+-29 s teleop vs 31+-27 s manual; tip-to-leak distance 3.0 +- 2.0 mm (operator registration) and 2.9 +- 1.5 mm (autonomous) (Results)
sim_model: none found (a data-replay simulator of recorded in vivo images and trajectories was used to develop the navigation software, Fig. 5; it is not a mechanics model of the robot)
